A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-SLIM work. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material support reliable comparison; the two supplementary pages are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, masking and component ablations in Tables 1–5, and qualitative attention analyses in Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds Qwen3-8B evaluations with and without 3D-SLIM in Table 2.

M1.justification: The geometry-adaptive mask, instruction-aware mask, training objective, and inference procedure remain operationally unchanged. Equation (1) changes an additive density constant from 1 to sqrt(3), but this shift cancels under the existing min–max normalization, preserving neighbor selection and masking.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA, and SQA3D on the same grounding, captioning, and question-answering tasks. Adding a decoder backbone does not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Qwen3-8B-Instruct without 3D-SLIM as a comparator alongside its augmented counterpart. The existing Vicuna, Llama3, and Qwen2 comparisons and all Table 1 comparators remain.

E3.justification: The decoder evaluation adds a Qwen3-8B-Instruct configuration within Chat-Scene. Previously reported configurations, dataset splits, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 extends the analysis of effectiveness across decoder backbones to Qwen3-8B. The masking-strategy, component, and neighborhood-range ablations in Tables 3–5 and qualitative analyses in Figures 4–5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional Qwen3 results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds two Qwen3 result rows: baseline/3D-SLIM ScanRefer Acc@0.5 is 51.5/55.8, and Multi3DRefer F1@0.5 is 56.5/59.6. These are newly reported configurations; all previously reported numerical entries in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4, Equation (1), revises the unnormalized density definition from 1 minus mean distance to sqrt(3) minus mean distance. This limited formal revision leaves normalized density unchanged; the remaining mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying causal-mask conflicts and addressing them through parameter-free geometry-adaptive and instruction-aware masking. Qwen3 supplies additional support for the existing generality claim.

C2.justification: The expanded cabinet-example explanation in Section 5.4 restates the existing interpretation that relational attention enables correct grounding while isolated-object attention fails. No substantive new mechanism, limitation, or applicability boundary is introduced; supplementary interpretations are identical.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that code is available and supplies a repository link in the abstract. The implementation details in Section 5.2, including optimization, batch sizes, neighborhood bounds, and hardware, are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen3 technical report as reference 22 for the newly evaluated decoder. Existing cited works and the positioning of decoder masking relative to input-representation research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgements and a code-availability sentence, updates the decoder discussion, and modestly expands the cabinet-example prose. The section organization and overall narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands by two rows, Table 1 is displayed at a smaller size, and surrounding text and references reflow. Figures 1–5 and their substantive captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added controlled Qwen3 comparison modestly strengthens evidence for the existing decoder-compatibility claim, while the repository pointer improves reproducibility information. Earlier results and supplementary analyses are preserved. The density-definition revision leaves masking behavior unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to stronger empirical support and documentation.
